clue.text: Request to obtain external sealing, device

indicators.note: external says the word for obtain sits on the outside, wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: to obtain is to get
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be given an outside seal for some piece of equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'sealing' is a stray mark on the printed page; the definition is 'sealing device'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ring or shaped sheet that seals a joint is exactly what this component is, a synonym.

clue.text: Basic principle that governs spectators' conduct at Lord's?

definitions.text: Basic principle that governs spectators' conduct at Lord's?

parts.words: Basic principle that governs spectators' conduct at Lord's?
parts.note: a basic principle, but literally a regulation of the venue for spectators at the famous London cricket venue

explanation.surface: Some rule tells cricket fans how to behave.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground, so its regulations are literally the rules of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A basic principle governing how something is done is the idiomatic sense of this phrase.

clue.text: Give out letters for a short period

definitions.meaning: to name the letters of a word in order
a brief stretch of time, as of weather

explanation.surface: Something is handed out letters for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both naming letters in order and a brief stint or bout of time.

clue.text: Serious listener needing somewhere cosy

parts.note: the ear is the organ of listening
a nest is a snug place

explanation.surface: A solemn person who listens wants a snug retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sincere and intense in manner is the synonym here.

clue.text: Holiday island has no good old pubs around

indicators.note: around says the word for pubs goes round the other pieces

parts.note: pubs are bars
no good means bad

explanation.surface: A tourist complains that a Caribbean island lacks decent traditional pubs nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' reads as part of a complaint about the pubs, but it is a piece of wordplay, and 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This Caribbean country is a popular holiday destination and an island, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Like the woman getting Jacob's son

parts.note: like means as
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman marries the son of the biblical Jacob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this is one of the twelve sons of Jacob, founder of a tribe of Israel.

clue.text: American friend and I brought in to manage African territory

indicators.note: brought in to says the word for manage goes into the other pieces

parts.note: bud is American slang for friend
to manage is to run

explanation.surface: A US pal and I are recruited to run an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: Bud is chiefly American, which is why the clue specifies an American friend.
explanation.definitionFit: This landlocked central African country is an example of a territory in Africa.

clue.text: Where there's a Newcastle and European queen

definitions.text: Where there's a Newcastle and European queen

parts.note: County Down in Northern Ireland contains a town called Newcastle
und is German, a European language, for and
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: A place with a town named Newcastle and a European monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes Australia, which has a Newcastle and had a European queen as head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal phrase names Australia, which has a city called Newcastle and a British monarch.

clue.text: Betray small political group in speech

indicators.note: in speech says a word is spoken aloud and the entry matches its sound

parts.note: a cell is a small group of political activists

explanation.surface: A little faction is accused of treachery during an address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' says CELL is spoken; the entry sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray someone, as in to sell them out, is an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: It's obvious two friends outside back of club will be having drug

parts.note: a pal is a friend, and there are two of them

indicators.note: outside says the friends go round the letter from club

parts.note: the second pal of the pair

indicators.note: back of picks the last letter of club

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: Clearly two mates hanging about outside a nightclub will be taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts PAL + PAL round B, the last letter of 'club'; 'will be having' is a link before E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evident enough to be felt or seen is a synonym, matching 'obvious'; 'It's' sits in the definition as a fragment of phrase.

clue.text: Where to see river bird go too far

definitions.meaning: a bird of the river is seen flying above a stretch of water, a phrase splitting into a preposition and a river stretch
to exceed one's limits, as a verb

explanation.surface: Birdwatching advice slides into a warning against going to excess.
explanation.walkthrough: A reach is a straight stretch of river, so a river bird is seen 'over reach'; run together, that phrase is the verb meaning to go too far.
explanation.definitionFit: To try for more than one can manage, overstepping limits, is the plain verb sense.

clue.text: Goad the Spanish to quarrel

parts.note: a quarrel is a row
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spaniards are being provoked into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are given in the reverse of answer order; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the spiked wheel on a spur, used to goad a horse, so the noun names a goad.

clue.text: Don't give up if you're doing Latin!

definitions.text: Don't give up if you're doing Latin!

parts.words: Don't give up if you're doing Latin!
parts.note: read as encouragement to a struggling Latin student, but really asks for the Latin phrase meaning never despair

explanation.surface: A teacher urges a pupil not to abandon their Latin studies.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin motto translates as 'never despair', the same message as 'don't give up'.

clue.text: Aware unpleasant woman can get tied into knots when upset

indicators.note: get tied into says the woman is placed inside the other piece
in a down clue, upset turns the word for knots upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: nodes are knots, as in a plant stem
a witch is an unpleasant woman

explanation.surface: An alert but nasty woman can get her knots tangled when she is in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when upset' turns the knots word upside down, which in a down clue means read backwards, giving SEDON; 'can' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and up to date is the informal sense of this phrase, a synonym for aware.

clue.text: Do repair job on man on field with it

parts.note: the referee is the official on a football field, ref for short

explanation.surface: A referee is asked to fix something out on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul or restore something, especially a ship or building, is a verb synonym for repair.

clue.text: Supporter of old-fashioned society creating bitter hostility over a border

parts.note: a feud is long and bitter hostility
a list is a strip of border or selvage on cloth

explanation.surface: A medieval-minded traditionalist stirs up hatred along a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: A list in this sense is the edge strip of woven cloth, a selvage; 'creating' and 'over' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone favouring the medieval system of lords and vassals backs an outdated social order.

clue.text: Dog kept outside home finally found niche inside it?

indicators.note: the dog is kept outside, so its word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: bow-wow is the nursery word for a dog
in means at home

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of found

explanation.surface: A dog is left outside while someone at home finds a cosy nook indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'it', the home in the wordplay: the window bulges out and makes a nook inside the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved bay projecting from a wall makes an alcove or niche within the room, a cryptic description.

clue.text: More than one fiasco was without cheer maybe

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: was goes round the other piece

parts.note: a shout is an example of a cheer

explanation.surface: Something counted as a flop for lack of applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it carries its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: These are failures or flops, plural to match 'more than one', an informal synonym.

clue.text: The Parisian's nakedness — who's got her clothes?

parts.note: la is French for the, as a Parisian would say it
undress is a state of nakedness

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman has been left naked and asks who has taken her clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ''s' is a link, standing for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A washerwoman has customers' clothes while she cleans them, a cryptic description of her trade.

clue.text: Across the nation, celebrated at last with style, raised to peerage

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of celebrated

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom, the nation

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised turns the word for style upwards, reading it backwards

parts.note: mode is a style

explanation.surface: A celebrity gets ennobled nationwide in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised to peerage' looks like the definition, but 'raised' reverses the style word, giving EDOM; 'with' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank of a duke is one of the grades of the nobility, an example of a peerage.

clue.text: Swagger shows confidence with son coming to the fore

indicators.note: the letter for son is moved to the front of the word

parts.note: confidence is trust

explanation.surface: A boastful walk displays self-assurance as a son steps forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to the fore' moves the S of TRUST to the front; 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A swagger and this showy walk are synonyms, both verbs for strutting proudly.

clue.text: One may have to put deal through the right processes

definitions.text: One may have to put deal through the right processes

parts.words: One may have to put deal through the right processes
parts.note: sounds like a business deal needing paperwork, but deal is pine timber being cut

explanation.surface: Someone must push a business agreement through proper procedures.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is softwood timber, such as pine or fir planks.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory that saws logs into planks processes deal timber, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Town near battle site with various tombs and earthwork

indicators.note: various signals the letters are rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: A historic battlefield town is surrounded by graves and old earthworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges TOMBS + EARTHWORK; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This Leicestershire market town lies beside Bosworth Field, where Richard III was killed in 1485.

clue.text: Martin's home from extended trips

definitions.meaning: St Martin was bishop of the French city on the Loire bearing this name

explanation.surface: Martin comes back home after long journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the French city of St Martin and long journeys around places.

clue.text: Bit of chopper showing decay given gold

parts.note: decay is rot
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Part of a helicopter is rusting and gets gilded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' and 'given' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter, a chopper, has this rotating blade assembly as a part.

clue.text: Made gesture of contempt in petty quarrel

definitions.meaning: expelled saliva in scorn, past tense

explanation.surface: Someone sneered during a trivial row.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of spit, a gesture of scorn, and a minor tiff.

clue.text: Heard a group of lions and was inquisitive

indicators.note: heard signals that a word is spoken and the entry matches its sound

parts.note: a group of lions is a pride

explanation.surface: Someone overheard lions and became curious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' says PRIDE is spoken; the entry is its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke into someone's affairs nosily is the past tense of a verb for prying, a synonym.

clue.text: Virginal Aunt Enid surprisingly catches gent finally

indicators.note: catches says the anagram holds the other letter inside it
surprisingly signals the letters of the words that follow are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of gent

explanation.surface: An innocent aunt unexpectedly gets hold of a gentleman at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges AUNT ENID, and 'catches' puts T, the last letter of 'gent', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something virginal is pure and unspoiled, a synonym for unsullied.

clue.text: One coming to object in an act of devotion?

definitions.text: One coming to object in an act of devotion?

parts.words: One coming to object in an act of devotion?
parts.note: looks like a protester, but means a worshipper who approaches a sacred object reverently

explanation.surface: Someone turns up to protest during a religious service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' is not a verb of protest but a noun: a totem is a sacred object.
explanation.definitionFit: A believer in totemism venerates a sacred emblem or object, so devotion to it describes him.

clue.text: No way for shopkeeper to take new coin

indicators.note: no says the letters for way are dropped from the shopkeeper

parts.note: a florist is a shopkeeper selling flowers
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper refuses to accept a newly minted coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes ST from FLORIST; 'to take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a British coin worth two shillings, an example of a coin.
